engagement_background.objective: Generate enterprise-wide procurement cost savings and leverage APDerm’s purchasing power across multiple locations to support private-equity value creation during a period of rising costs and supply-chain disruption.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Two-phase strategic sourcing program covering roughly $6.3 million in annual baseline spend across 10+ indirect categories (e.g., billing services, janitorial, IT managed services, medical & office supplies, courier, telecom). Waste Management was later excluded when a new contract limited savings potential.
constraints_challenges: Highly decentralized buying across many New England clinic locations acquired over time, resulting in a fragmented supplier base
Limited spend visibility and inconsistent contract records, requiring extensive data cleansing and mapping of AP datasets
Inflationary market conditions and pandemic-related supply-chain issues putting upward pressure on prices
Need to minimize operational disruption by retaining incumbents where possible, reducing flexibility to switch suppliers
Aggressive timeline tied to private-equity value-creation targets for realizing savings

procurement_environment.data_availability: Accounts-payable spend extracts, GL reports, and supplier usage data were available but scattered; no centralized contract repository.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Duplicate vendor names, unmapped GL codes, and gaps in usage data required significant cleansing (evident in ‘Vendor Dedupe’, ‘Vendor Map’, and notes about incomplete supplier responses).

extraction_notes: Objective and challenges explicitly stated on pages 2–3 of the case-study PDF.
Decentralized operating model confirmed in case study (‘purchasing was decentralized’).
